findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. Previously the whole delete was scoped to SMS. Now any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 is deleted, regardless of method. Other cron jobs (email, WhatsApp) may start using retryCount, and their reminders would then be deleted by the SMS cron. Add `method: SMS` to that branch.

findings.title: Catch-block update can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch is not guarded. If it fails (for example the row was deleted concurrently, or the DB is unavailable), the exception escapes the for-loop. The remaining reminders are then not processed and the handler returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Threshold `gt: 1` does not match the description and is delayed by a run
findings.body: The PR says reminders are deleted after two failed attempts. The deletion runs at the start of the next cron run, and only for retryCount > 1. A reminder that fails twice reaches retryCount 2 and is deleted on the third run. Reminders that never reach the send branch (no message or no sendTo) never increment the count and are retried until the scheduled date, which is the behaviour the PR aims to remove.
